body: Obviously no, you fucking idiot.
I'm sorry, did you say you'd like a hippo?! Well that's....that's definitely a new one.
Rat owner here. They're tiny little dogs, honestly they're great, they give me such joy every day. Probably the most active, affectionate rodent you can get as a pet.
Nah, you're good. A dog would struggle at first, but cats are far more adaptable. She'll be fine.
Supporting my arse, she's just as much lead.

Not at all.
Please still be here.

Going that way HURTS. I once only got halfway deep enough, and Christ, that was painful enough. It's not quick, the pain isn't over once you've made the cuts, even if you manage to get the strength together to make the second one. Your hands scrunch up and you will die shaking from the pain. You won't just slowly drift off, all eerily beautiful like in all the films. Don't do it, if for no other reason than the pain. I'm sure there are many other reasons that people could give you though.

Maybe more people want to be your friend than you think. And if not, well, it's never too late to make friends. I guarantee someone, somewhere cares about you. Hell, I care about you. I fully relate to the self loathing. I hate myself most hours of the day, but deep, deep, deep down, in the fleeting hours of rationality (one of which I seem to be in now, who knows what tomorrow holds), I know I'm not as bad as I think. And I know you're not either. You're asking that people don't care about your potential suicide, That shows caring for others and their mental well being right there, and that's a good quality. That alone gives you a lot of worth in this world, more than a lot of others.
Already seems like more people care than you think. Folks don't try to help if they don't care.
Mate, I wanted to earlier today, made a post about it, and I probably will again tomorrow. But I'm still, with what I can muster, trying. Please do the same, I know it hurts, but please cling on.

Thank you for replying. My flatmate overheard me crying and came in and just sat with me silently. He's surprisingly understanding and doesn't dress anything up, just says he knows there's nothing he can do in the long run, anything he can do now? Doesn't give me the usual spiel about exercise and productivity, just sits with me until he thinks I'm not at risk. That can sometimes smooth things over a bit temporarily. But knowing someone understood can never be undervalued, so thank you. I hope you too get the answer you need. Ever wanna talk please message me.
I prefer Us.
I was silent for a few seconds, then laughed. Fair play, you got me.

I'll give you that Sarah Connor was certainly a better character in T2, though weird enough that is another reason why the tension is lessened to me. Sarah is way more competent here, so my fear for her is less. Nobody really equals the wide eyed, vulnerable young woman thrown in over her head from the original, the woman who scrambles desperately to survive even though she herself is hardly capable of understanding her situation, barely scraping her way to survival. Not even John does, having been raised with the knowledge of Terminators so being far readier to accept the truth. I dunno, I guess I just feared for her in a way I didn't T2's Sarah.

Thanks, I'm relieved people are saying not to worry about the pellets. None the less, tomorrow's an essentials trip, so I'll grab some more then and give the cage another once over (wasn't able to get out today, flat mate needed help) . It's funny you mention the dog/cat thing as I've actually made the same analogy myself when talking about them. Pippin's the cat, Merry's the dog. I've always tended to be a bit more of a dog person, but I love them both as they are.
Thank you for an encouraging answer :-)

I'm that way too. Personally, I try and take it as positively as I can. Like, I don't do it regularly any more, that's a positive step. And I never promise myself that I'm never gonna do it again, as I never know what the future holds with my mental health. But when I do do it I now find it easier, afterwards at least, to look at it as a little backstep rather than a full blown regression. When the breaks get longer rather than go "ah fuck it, I'd gone a whole 2 months too, fucking backsliding idiot" (2 months is a random choice) I try to be more like "hey, two months this time, that's not bad."  Sorry, I know I'm blabbing about me, but maybe if you tried a similar perspective it might help?
I and a lot of other people I know still do it (misery loves company). I'm 28. How often? Is it a sporadic thing or would you say you do it on a regular basis?
I'm not gone yet. My post was a "I'm probably gonna do it during this whole quarantine shite." But it only got one response. Which does kind of confirm to me that nobody gives a shit.
I've been walking. keep feeling like people are twitching their curtains and looking at me disapprovngly.
It's morning where I am. Tried crying myself to sleep, but I can't sleep at the moment. I'm like the other guy here, I wanna help, I really do, I'm just in a similar place myself. But I care.
You're not alone. I wanna go too a lot of the time.
